title: Swift Package Manager, dependencies and the toolchain

videos.script: Lessons 17 and 18 used packages. This one opens one up. {{anatomy}} First, what swift package init makes. A manifest that is a Swift program, a Sources directory, and a first line that is not a comment. {{targets}} Then the planner's own package. Targets are how you organise it. Products are what you promise to everybody else. {{deps}} Then a dependency from GitHub, Apple's argument parser. Two lines of manifest, and the program gains options, a help page and errors that make sense. {{resolved}} Then the file that says which version is really in use. You will watch it hold a version still, until you ask it to move. {{release}} Then debug against release. Release is faster and smaller, and it also quietly drops a check. {{toolchain}} And last, three version numbers that look alike: the compiler's, the manifest's, and the language mode. By the end, the planner is a package with a library, a tool, and one dependency you chose on purpose.
